data.revised_prompt:
Create a clean, publication-ready VECTOR-STYLE neural network architecture diagram for a split-stem recurrent policy used in active depth sensing for quadrotor navigation. Wide landscape layout, 3840 x 1280 aspect ratio, white background, centered composition, aligned rectangular modules, left-to-right data flow, with three horizontal bands: top band flight branch, middle-left band depth encoding, bottom band camera branch. Use crisp thin black/dark gray arrows and text, subtle pastel fills, no shadows, no 3D, no decorative art, no icons, no photorealism.

Overall structure:
- Left side input feeds into depth encoding.
- From depth encoding, the pipeline splits into two independent branches: flight branch on top and camera branch on bottom.
- Branches visually separate and balanced with white space.
- Use a muted red dashed outline around the entire camera branch area and label it “frozen during flight-only”.

Depth encoding band (light blue fill):
- Input box labeled “D_obs”.
- Next box labeled “Depth encoding”. Inside or immediately beneath it, indicate two channels: “near inv-depth max-pool” and “far metric-range avg-pool”.
- Output box labeled “Phi_t (2 ch., 12x16)”.
- Arrows: D_obs -> Depth encoding -> Phi_t (2 ch., 12x16).

Flight branch (green fill):
- From Phi_t, flow to box labeled “F_f stem”. Show inside/under it the short label “Conv 32-64-128, AvgPool 3x6, 192-D”.
- Parallel input from left or from a shared flight-state input box labeled “s_t” into a box labeled “W_s state proj” producing 192-D.
- Feed both 192-D streams into “LayerNorm + Gated fusion” (use two inputs converging to this fusion box).
- Then to “GRU_f” with a small note “residual LN” and a hidden-state transition label “h_t -> h_{t+1}”.
- Final output box in soft purple labeled “W_u” and output label “u_t”.
- Keep flight branch strictly independent from camera branch after the shared depth encoding.

Camera branch (orange fill, inside dashed frozen outline):
- From Phi_t, flow to box labeled “F_c stem”. Show inside/under it the same layout short label “Conv 32-64-128, AvgPool 3x6, 192-D”. Make it clear this is copy-initialized but independent from F_f.
- Then to “G_c adapter” box with short internal description “Conv 2->4->4, Pool 2x3”.
- Then to “residual image adapter” box labeled “A_c” and output label “z_t^c”.
- In parallel, camera-side state inputs: a box labeled “c_t, m_t” feeding into two embedding boxes labeled “W_c” and “W_m”, with small labels “24-D” for each, then concatenate with z_t^c.
- Concatenate inputs into a box labeled “W_p” with output “96-D”.
- Then to “GRU_c” with hidden-state transition label “q_t -> q_{t+1}”.
- Final output box in soft purple labeled “W_o” and output label “c*_{t+1}=[P,E,G]”.
- Use a sigmoid tag near W_o.

Label requirements:
Use only short, readable labels. Keep labels large and horizontal. Use exact short labels such as: “D_obs”, “Depth encoding”, “Phi_t (2 ch., 12x16)”, “F_f stem”, “s_t”, “Gated fusion”, “GRU_f”, “u_t”, “F_c stem”, “G_c adapter”, “z_t^c”, “c_t, m_t”, “W_c, W_m”, “W_p”, “GRU_c”, “c*_{t+1}=[P,E,G]”, “frozen during flight-only”.

Style details:
- Flat vector infographic suitable for SCI journal method figure.
- Crisp edges, aligned rectangular modules, consistent spacing.
- Light blue for depth encoding, green for flight branch, orange for camera branch, soft purple for outputs, muted red dashed stroke for frozen outline.
- Black or dark gray text and arrows.
- No extra modules, no paragraphs, no misspellings, no overlapping arrows, no clutter.
- Ensure the camera branch includes both F_c stem and G_c adapter, and both c_t and m_t inputs.
- Ensure F_f and F_c are clearly independent stems, not shared.
